studies.title: Thermodynamic Bounds and an Optimal Tempo for Goal-Holding Agents
studies.short_title: Thermodynamic Bounds and an Optimal Tempo
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Defines an agent as a system that holds a goal under an energy budget, derives physical bounds on how fast it can act per second and per joule, and reads intelligence as progress per joule on a completed run. Plain words: to count as an agent, a system must aim at a goal, act, and stay within an energy budget; physics sets a minimum energy cost for every decision; among systems that finish a job correctly, the one that used less energy ranks higher.

studies.title: Metered Commit Gates: Energy-to-Correct-Completion for Agentic Systems
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: A gate that lets a machine act only after a check passes, and a cascade that tries the cheapest method first, with software results and one board-level energy reading (11,428 pJ per gate cycle, whole module, KV260). Plain words: do not take an action that cannot be undone until a check says it is safe; try the cheapest way first; write every decision down with its energy.

studies.title: Deterministic Null: A Pre-Registered Control Experiment for Neural and Agentic Substrates
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Constructs and pre-registers a zero-model-call 64-bit integer case loop (Shape D: strict N0 and dev-crystallized N1, verified bit-exact across Rust, C++20, Go, Julia, and Python in openIE-dev/deterministic-null) under OpenTimestamps Bitcoin Calendar proofs and League of Entropy drand randomness rounds (6663734 and 6664089), and measures the paired increment of Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, OpenAI gpt-oss-120b, xAI Grok 4.20, Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B, and Gemma 4 E4B-it across 4,030 held-out instances and 6 real upstream SWE-bench Verified repositories. Bounded formal and structured classes exclude single-turn neural relevance on 9 of 10 Track-A cells while extended-thinking (49/50) and O(m) clause feedback (50/50) close Unique 3-SAT DRAT; unique external public benchmarks (BFCL v3, tau-bench Retail, BigCodeBench v0.1.3, SWE-bench Verified) show +45.80 to +95.00 percentage-point neural increments while online Zipfian crystallization cuts calls and reported_j spend by 3.59x. Local Apple M5 Max counters are reported_j; no rail or wall power monitor was attached.

studies.title: Satiation Benchmark: Reference Harness, Adapters, and Telemetry Attribution
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Specifies and empirically audits the Satiation Benchmark (SATB) evaluation stack: a deterministic sequential Rust reference harness (Lane B with ContextRule_v0 80% oldest-tool-output elision and Truncate_v0 8+8 KiB truncation), a loopback proxy bridge (Shapes D, M, H, and I), a five-block SUT fingerprint, twelve conformance checks (C1-C12), and a five-level rootless telemetry engine (L0-L4 crossed with attribution labels A1-N). Measured on Apple M5 Max: 12/12 C1-C12 checks pass (0-byte replay drift across 149,747 B, 2.073 ms process-group SIGKILL cleanup, 24/24 and 6/6 multi-file completion parity with Claude Code 2.1.330 at 1.67x-3.44x lower token traffic); live C12 probes across Anthropic, Cerebras, and xAI expose HTTP 400 temperature=0 deprecation on Claude 5.5 and residual seed=42 variance on cloud inference; boundary rusage reads draw 0.011 mW vs 66.44 mW at 10 Hz; CPU-proportional Kepler splits diverge from exact sequential boundary counters by 32.59%-35.86% on L2; and Falsifier 6 drops 124/188 drifted shared-host net baselines while preserving 100% of raw L2 and L3 reported_j counters. Plain words: one fixed Rust wrapper holds context and tool policy constant, one local proxy logs every external agent call, and each energy sensor stays labelled by its true boundary without guessing closed-API server joules.

studies.title: Time as an Index: What It Would Take to Look Up Tomorrow
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Tests the premise that sequential brute-force search is safe only because future states are unindexed across CTC complexity (D-CTC = PSPACE, P-CTC = PP, unbounded Delta_2), quantum no-signalling, analog relaxation, Hellman precomputation (T*M^2 = N^2), 31 Lean 4.36.0 kernel-checked theorems (Horizon.lean and Paradox.lean, zero sorry), deterministic M1 to M8 and F5 SHA-256 spectral runs (N = 65,536 digests, 0 bins below corrected p = 10^-6), and 195 cataloged temporal anomalies (TA001-TA081), frequency edge cases (AA01-AA40), and paradoxes (P01-P74). Plain words: inside a mathematical time loop almost every math-based cipher breaks at once, leaving only one-time pads; in known physics nothing reads tomorrow early, every real lookup is precomputation paid ahead of time, and fresh salts or block hashes stop tables from starting before the question exists. No hardware power monitor was attached (board_metered is false).

studies.title: Downward LUT6 Compilation in a Mixture of Limits Cascade: Beneš-Routed Boolean Fabrics, Conformal Wake Gates, and 4-Bit NVMe Layer Streaming
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Places a reconfigurable 6-input truth-table (LUT6) lookup tier in front of Mamba-3 and 4-bit NVMe-streamed 2026 hybrid models (LiquidAI/LFM2.5-350M and Qwen/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base), and compiles certified wakes downward into 81-RAMB36E2 Beneš-routed lookup pages at openIE-dev/lut-adapt-ai (commit 9dbf745). Reports measured Darwin F_NOCACHE NVMe byte counts (2.86 and 2.74 tokens per sweep post-wake at 100.0% exact token parity), active RAM (128.0 MB and 242.5 MB), Yosys/Verilator xck26 RTL simulation (41,186 CLB LUTs, 81 RAMB36E2s, 0 DSP48s, CPI = 1.0), and analytical est_j estimates. No board power was measured. Plain words: repeated model work is compiled into cheap table lookups only after a check passes; streaming a 2026 model from disk with that zero-FLOP drafter cuts disk reads by nearly three times without changing a single output token.

studies.title: Task Satiation vs. Aggregate Rebound in AI Demand
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Defines the stop at which more machine work on a finished task adds nothing, and separates it from growth in total demand. Plain words: every job has a finish line; cheaper work can still create more jobs; AI prices fall but its electricity is never free.

studies.title: The Reality Code Engine: One Lossless Form for Native, Verified, Low-Energy Programming
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: A system in which a program is written once as a state machine and code in other languages is generated from it: its specification (openIE-dev/rce at 1762fb4b), reference checker and emitters, 5,537 Lean 4 kernel theorem constants (theorems T1 to T63), 2,221/2,236 passing conformance checks with 0 failures, Apple M5 Max reported_j checker receipts (49.04 mJ per Form check; measured_j unset), and registered measurements of program dimension. Plain words: a program is written once and generated in many languages; the language requires every input to have a declared outcome; in the engine's design, checked fixes are saved so that the same problem is not paid for twice.

studies.title: RCE-JEPA: World Coding, with JEPA as Premise
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: World Coding, with JEPA (a Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) as the premise rather than the whole method. Any learned proposer may suggest a Form. The checker decides. Measured floors: median rho 9.34 over 185 hand-written programs, 0 violations in 1,275 fuzzed mutants, 0 mismatches on 10,500 streams across six targets, H2 supported on Apple M5 Max reported_j (49.04 mJ per Form check vs 84.25 J local Qwen 3.6 proposal, ratio 0.000582), and a ladder that closed 111 of 151 tasks (73.5%) with zero model calls. On the 40 residual tasks (H15, k = 1), Claude Opus 5.5 admits 34/40 (85.0%), Claude Sonnet 5.5 32/40, xAI Grok 4.20 Reasoning 31/40, OpenAI GPT-OSS-120B 29/40, and local Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B 27/40, while Shape D (DNULLMM1) Gear-0 replays 34/40 at 0 calls (1.77 uJ lookup), hits 7/9 alpha-renamed tasks via rce fmt nameless, and cuts Zipf(0.85) calls by 4.17x. No purpose-trained latent Form JEPA has been trained yet. The Laws of Coding are the acceptance rule under test, not a result claimed for other systems.

studies.title: RCE Compile: A Law of Compilation, Tested as a Normal Form Against Real Compilers
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Asks whether one statement of what compilation is holds for any compiler, independent of the Reality Code Engine. Checked against twelve compiler families, it fails as a description and holds as a normal form: seven parts (representation, lowering, cost, checker, reuse, energy, gate), four equivalence levels, a gate that names its property, linking assumption, trusted base, evidence authority and digests, and a measurable replacement for the Landauer and Kolmogorov bounds. Experiments so far: byte comparisons of compiler outputs on three machines; erasure and description-length counts with no energy read; and a name-free hash that matched renamed programs more often than byte or source-text keys, with no false match, on 16 small kernels and 4 programs. Plain words: real compilers do not all obey one rule, so the rule becomes a standard each compiler can be measured against; none of them tracks energy.

studies.title: RCE-VC: Law of Version Control
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: A reference for the Law of Version Control: each change is admitted to one name-free repository state or refused with a recorded reason, and Git stays usable. Milestones M0 to M2 are in openIE-dev/rce-vc at commit aba99fce (49 offline tests). On Apple M5 Max, one core admitted a submission against 100,000 units in 69.7 to 73.6 microseconds at 317 to 365 microjoules of L3 reported_j (measured_j is unset). Receipt costs also carry the stated est_uj table. The reference is not the Reality Code Engine language. Plain words: a named check admits or a written reason refuses; changes that do not overlap need no coordination; a writer can stay on Git.

studies.title: Writing a Game Once and Running It Everywhere: Where Exact Replay Ends and Tolerance Begins
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Asks whether a game can be written once as a checked state machine and projected into several engines and languages, with an IR table, a layer split (simulation, scripting, scene, rendering), a determinism boundary, and executed GE-H1 and GE-H2 benchmarks on Apple M5 Max: 100,000 ticks of 64 Q32.32 fixed-point bodies across Rust native, Rust Wasm32, C++20, Node.js BigInt, and Python 3.13 produce 0/1,000 SHA-256 checkpoint mismatches (0.103 J Rust to 13.60 J Python L3 reported_j; measured_j unset), while IEEE-754 float controls diverge at tick 1 (f32), tick 37 (libm vs V8 Math.sin), and tick 192 (FMA). Cross-ISA x86-64 parity and GE-H3 to GE-H9 remain open. Plain words: game rules replay bit-identically across five runtimes when integer arithmetic is pinned down, while standard floats drift within ticks; pictures cannot be identical on every graphics card and require tolerance checks.

studies.title: The Pursuit of AGI Resolves the Three-Body Problem in Computing
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Locates many computing failures at handoffs between the people who specify, build and use systems, states when checking every handoff assumption makes a stack stable, and supports it with independently tested verified systems (CompCert, seL4, TLA+ at AWS, unit types). Plain words: most big failures happen at handoffs; the cause is usually an unwritten guess; if every guess is written down and machine-checked, a fix stays fixed.

studies.title: "AI" Reads Human: Human Language Encoding at Machine Speed and the Energy Cost
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Software agents exchange data in formats made for people to read. This study names the extra work that causes (the impedance tax), defines it with units, and measures parse time, token counts, and Apple M5 Max dual-channel reported_j across 34 parse and tiktoken workloads on a reproducible 20,000-record corpus (170 isolated windows): L3 per-process parsing spans 2,053.8x from 280.4 nJ/record (fixed binary struct) to 2,212.1 nJ/record (stdlib JSON, 7.89x), 69,922.1 nJ/record (C libyaml, 249.4x), and 575,799.3 nJ/record (pure-Python YAML), while cl100k_base JSON tokenization costs 27,678.7 nJ/record (12.51x json.loads). Shared-host L2 IOReport triggers Falsifier 6 on 109/170 windows; measured_j is unset. Plain words: people and computers share one written format, and the computer pays extra time, tokens, and chip energy to read it.

studies.title: Spell Check is Global: The Future of Computer Intelligence in the Hands of the Many (7B+), Not the Few
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Documents with dated prices how spell check went from a premium product to a free built-in feature, and explains it by marginal cost and bundling. Plain words: spell check used to cost a lot and is now free; it became free because it costs almost nothing to run and is most useful inside tools people have; other computer skills can follow.

studies.title: The Promised Trillion Dollar AI-Coding Market
studies.short_title: The Promised Trillion Dollar AI-Coding Market
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Lists who projects a trillion-dollar AI coding market, labels each number by kind, and names the shared assumptions about energy, tokens and reuse, with testable propositions. Plain words: the big numbers are mostly forecasts; they assume a large model is paid for every piece of code forever; reuse would lower the cost of repeated work toward the cost of electricity.

studies.title: The Price of the Unexamined Interface
studies.short_title: The Price of the Unexamined Interface
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Published costs of failures at handoffs, labeled as accounted costs, model estimates or survey estimates and never added into one total. Plain words: some handoff failures have exact price tags; national totals are estimates; checking assumptions is cheap but the one who does it pays while everyone benefits.

studies.title: Metabolic Intelligence: Budget-Native Compute from Tag to Campus
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: Computer intelligence designed to run inside a fixed energy budget, with emulator counts and a datasheet schedule for a cold-chain sensor tag and a protocol test of a grid-following data center. No external energy meter. Plain words: give a computer a fixed energy budget and design it for the best answer inside it; a datasheet schedule for a food sensor tag comes out near eight years on a coin battery, and that figure is not a bench rundown; a data center model can cut power when the grid asks without giving wrong answers.

studies.title: The Search for JouleOS
studies.kind: Product white paper (review and design guide)
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: A review of how operating systems, instruction sets and agent sandboxes are composed today, and checkable requirements for a machine that schedules, meters and refuses an agent under an energy budget. Plain words: AI agents are added on top of old layers; none of them checks energy before an agent acts; a machine for agents should measure energy, budget it, and refuse what breaks the budget.

studies.title: The Gap Between Possible and Deployed: A Cadence Model of Computer Intelligence and the Forcing Function of Automation Tools
studies.short_title: The Gap Between Possible and Deployed
studies.author: David Charlot, Open Interface Engineering
studies.summary: A dated survey of methods that lower the cost of computer intelligence, evidence on the gap between publication and deployment, and a cadence model in which reporting and funding calendars quantize release decisions, with a forcing-function result for tools that lower the cost of automation. It adds what public filings document about capital flows among labs, clouds and chip makers with a closed-loop test, a cost model in dollars and joules per task, open methods and alternative hardware measured against the incumbent stack, and maps of compute, power and models. Plain words: cheaper methods are published long before most products use them; most of what a task costs is the machine and not the electricity; part of the wait is engineering and part is calendars; once the work is cheap, what is left to charge for is the cost of switching away.
